output:
I'll start by reading the docs and the package layout.

Output truncated in the middle; I'll read values.md and the start of functions.md.

My last call was cut off before it ran. I'll apply the fixes with a Python script.

I'll use smaller edits instead.

My last call had invalid JSON. I'll put the probe script in a file and run that.

The shell can write to `/tmp` even though `write_file` couldn't, so I'll create the probe script from the shell.

I fixed the bugs in `gridcalc` so it follows the docs. All 58 unit tests now pass (`python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`, OK), and `tools/check.py` reports no broken rules. I also ran about 50 formulas covering the edge cases in the docs, and they gave the documented results. I wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

What I fixed:
- **Numbers:** exponent numbers such as `1.5e3` now read as numbers, both in formulas and in text that holds a number. Numbers become text in `%.10g` form, so `0.1+0.2` is `0.3` and `12345678901` is `1.23456789e+10`.
- **Columns and ranges:** multi-letter columns were off (`AA` was column 1), and ranges written from any corner (`B3:A1`) now work.
- **Precedence:** prefix minus is now looser than `^`, and `^` groups from the right, so `-2^2` is -4 and `2^3^2` is 512.
- **Empty cells:** an undefined cell now reads as empty rather than 0, so `A9&"x"` is `x` and `COUNT(A9)` is 0.
- **Functions:**
  - `SUM`, `AVERAGE`, `MIN` and `MAX` skip text that holds a number inside a range.
  - `IF` only evaluates the branch it takes.
  - `ROUND` no longer fails on large values.
- **Output:**
  - Cells are in cell order (`A9, A10, …, Z3, AA1`) instead of string order.
  - Booleans are typed `bool` instead of `number`.
  - Refs listings no longer repeat entries.
- **Sheet files:** lines and contents are trimmed of spaces and tabs only, as `sheets.md` says.

Two places where the docs seem to disagree with themselves, and what I did:
- If a function gets both an error in a range and an error in a plain argument, `functions.md` 1.3 and 2.1 point in opposite directions. I kept the current behaviour, where plain-argument errors win (1.3).
- Text such as `1e999` holds a number but is not finite. I left it as text in a literal cell and as `#VALUE!` in arithmetic, because the docs don't say.

command_result.command: cd /app && find . -path ./.git -prune -o -type f -print | head -100 && cat docs/overview.md && wc -l gridcalc/*.py docs/* tests/*
cd /app && cat docs/sheets.md docs/formulas.md docs/values.md docs/functions.md docs/output.md docs/changelog.md; ls docs/archive tools; ls
cd /app && cat gridcalc/tokens.py gridcalc/parser.py gridcalc/refs.py gridcalc/values.py
cd /app && cat gridcalc/evaluate.py gridcalc/functions.py gridcalc/report.py gridcalc/sheets.py gridcalc/cli.py gridcalc/errors.py; sed -n 36,60p docs/functions.md
cd /app && sed -n 45,200p gridcalc/functions.py; sed -n 1,25p gridcalc/report.py; cat tools/check.py | head -50; git status 2>&1 | head -3
cd /app && grep -lP '\r' data/sheets/* | head; grep -lP '[^\x00-\x7f]' data/sheets/* | head; python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -40; cat tests/support.py tests/test_documents.py
cd /app && head -8 gridcalc/report.py; grep -n 'sorted\|bool' gridcalc/report.py; grep -n 'to_number(v)' gridcalc/functions.py; grep -n NUMBER gridcalc/tokens.py | head -2
cd /app && python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -40; python tools/check.py | tail -12
ls -ld /tmp /root; df /tmp | tail -1; touch /tmp/x && echo ok

cd /app && python -m gridcalc run --out /tmp/out && cat /tmp/out/errors.json; python -m gridcalc cell s-001 a1; printf 'A1: 1\r\nB1: x\n' > /tmp/d.sheet; mkdir -p /tmp/dd/sheets && cp /tmp/d.sheet /tmp/dd/sheets/q.sheet && python -m gridcalc show q --data /tmp/dd | head -20

cd /app && cat > STATUS.json <<'EOF'
{
  "status": "success",
  "summary": "Fixed gridcalc to follow the docs: exponent numbers, column indexing for multi-letter columns, normalized range containment, prefix-minus/^ precedence and right-grouping, %.10g number text, empty undefined cells, text skipped in SUM/AVERAGE/MIN/MAX ranges, lazy IF, ROUND precision, refs dedupe, cell-order sorting, bool typing, and exact space/tab stripping in sheet lines. All 58 unit tests and tools/check.py pass."
}
EOF
